issues.title: Roadmap: USG-3P IPv4 fast path (start here)
issues.body:
**Start here.** This is the map of all work on the CPU-assisted IPv4 fast path for the OpenBSD/octeon `cnmac(4)` driver on the Ubiquiti USG-3P. GitHub Issues are the source of truth for all work ([AGENTS.md]({{REPO_URL}}/blob/main/AGENTS.md)); the specification, design and decision record live in [`docs/`]({{REPO_URL}}/tree/main/docs).

Optimize routing and VLAN throughput and packet rate first. R13 is a milestone, not a stopping point: G3 must record the remaining bottlenecks and the next useful optimization, or evidence that the tested workload is at its link limit. Mode P is not a prerequisite. Phase 0 board work and Phase 1 run in parallel; Phase 2 starts only when its entry conditions are met.

### How the issues are organized

| Kind | Label | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| Epic | `epic` | One per phase; its sub-issues are that phase's tasks and gates. |
| Task | `task` | One former TASKS.md item (T*), with its verbatim Done-when. |
| Gate | `gate` | SPEC §7.1 hard stops G0–G3 and the decision each records. |
| User story | `user-story` | SPEC requirements R1–R16 (and mode P) under {{E-REQ}}. |
| Chore | `chore` | Infrastructure and tooling under {{E-INFRA}}. |
| Finding | `finding` | Doc or code discrepancies; resolved into ERRATA. |

`env:*` labels say what a task's Done-when needs: `env:board` (USG-3P and bench), `env:build-host` (OpenBSD host, {{C2}}), `env:desk` (this repository only). `needs-owner` marks decisions only the owner can make.

### Phases

```
Phase 0 (host/box) T0.1 pin ─ T0.2 build/boot ─ T0.3 bench ─ T0.4 baseline ─► [G0]
                 T0.5–T0.9 probes (any order after T0.2)
Phase 1 (amd64)  T1.0 build ─ T1.1 sysctl ─ T1.2 core ─ T1.3 gen ─ T1.4 mark ─ T1.5 vlan
                 ─ T1.6 learn ─ T1.7 GC/ARP ─ T1.8 mode switch
                 T1.9 amd64 harness develops alongside T1.5–T1.8
Phase 2 (box)    T2.1 MD glue ─ T2.2 HOOK B ─ T2.3 shadow ─► [G1] ─ T2.4 budget/yield ─► [G2]
                 ─ T2.5 mode 1 ─ T2.6..T2.10 tests + measure ─► [G3]
Phase 3 (opt.)   mode 2 zero-copy, only if G3 says so
Phase 4          hardening, soaks, README
```

Provision the OpenBSD build host (-current at the pinned commit)
issues.body:
Phase 1 and Phase 0 builds need an **OpenBSD -current build host at the pinned source version** ([DESIGN §7]({{DOC:DESIGN:7}})): a full checkout at `/usr/src`, matching installed headers and tools, permission to build there, and the `Makefile.cross` octeon toolchain. The amd64 VM also runs the T1.9 learn harness. Nothing like this exists yet; the development Mac (macOS, arm64) cannot run the build.

This blocks the Done-when of T0.1 (unmodified build), T0.2, T0.5–T0.9 (probe kernels) and every Phase 1 task. Code can be written before it exists.

### Options

1. **Separate amd64 machine or cloud VM** running an OpenBSD -current snapshot, then `make build` and a kernel from the pinned `/usr/src`, so host headers and tools match the fork point exactly. Matches DESIGN §7 as written. *Recommended.*
2. **QEMU on the Mac, amd64 guest under TCG emulation.** Matches DESIGN §7, but emulation makes every kernel build slow (hours), which hurts the Phase 1 edit-build-test loop.
3. **QEMU or UTM on the Mac, arm64 guest with hardware virtualization.** Fast, and the MI flow code is the same on arm64, but it changes DESIGN §7 and T1.9 (amd64), and cross-building octeon from an arm64 host is untested. Needs an ERRATA entry before use.

### Done when

- [ ] The host is reachable by agents (record the ssh alias or access method in AGENTS.md) with `/usr/src` at `c595b86dd344` plus the fork patches ({{C3}}).
- [ ] `config GENERIC.MP` and the DESIGN §7 recipe run, with tool versions recorded in NOTES.md (feeds {{T0.2}}).
- [ ] An amd64 GENERIC.MP kernel builds and boots in the VM (feeds {{T1.0}}).

Owner decision needed: which option, and who provisions it.

issues.title: Decide where the OpenBSD src fork lives
issues.body:
T0.1 says "Fork -current at `c595b86dd344`". Where the forked tree lives is not specified. Options:

1. **Patch series in this repository** (`patches/`, made with `git format-patch` against `c595b86dd344`), applied to a checkout of `openbsd/src` by `tools/fork-src.sh`. Small, private, and rebasing means re-applying the series to a newer upstream. **In use as the interim choice** so work can start; see the ruling on {{T0.1}}.
2. **Private mirror repository with full history.** Private and rebase-friendly, but upstream is about 1.7 GB and GitHub limits a single push to 2 GB, so the history has to be pushed in pieces.
3. **Public GitHub fork of `openbsd/src`.** Fastest and rebase-friendly, but GitHub forks of public repositories are public; SPEC §2 calls this a private, non-production fork.

Recommendation: keep option 1 until the build host exists ({{C2}}), then decide whether the build host should pull a branch instead.

### Done when

- [ ] Owner picks an option (comment here).
- [ ] AGENTS.md "Where code lives" matches the choice, and `tools/fork-src.sh` (or its replacement) reproduces the tree.

Starting T0.1 (desk part). Environment: macOS arm64 development Mac; no OpenBSD build host yet ({{C2}}).

issues.title: Finding: flow data structures do not belong in the hook-API header (DESIGN §4)
issues.body:
**Finding (low), found while starting {{T1.0}}.**

DESIGN §4 shows `struct flow_key`, `struct flow` and the priority/PCP constants under a `/* sys/net/if_flow.h */` banner, and DESIGN §3.1 lists `struct flow_md_ops` in the same header. But `if_flow.h` is also the hook API that every hook-site file includes (DESIGN §3, about twenty files: `route.c`, `rtsock.c`, `if.c`, `if_ethersubr.c`, `if_ether.c`, `ip_input.c`, `bpf.c`, `pf_ioctl.c`, …). With `pseudo-device flow` configured, each of them would then have to compile those structures, which need:

- `CACHELINESIZE`, defined on amd64 only by `sys/sys/percpu.h:22-23` (octeon gets 128 from `sys/arch/octeon/include/cpu.h:77` via `<sys/param.h>` → `machine/param.h` → `mips64/param.h:41`);
- `SMR_LIST_ENTRY` and `struct smr_entry` (`<sys/smr.h>`);
- `struct in_addr` (`<netinet/in.h>`) and `ETHER_ADDR_LEN` (`<netinet/if_ether.h>`).

Either every hook site grows four includes it does not otherwise use, or a missing include breaks the build only when flow is configured.

**Resolution:** keep `if_flow.h` to the sysctl names and the hook API (enum, hooks, `flow_sysctl`, `flowattach`, NFLOW stubs). Put the data structures, the MD operations and the internal MI/MD prototypes in a new `sys/net/if_flowvar.h`, included only by `if_flow.c`, `if_cnmac_flow.c` and ddb (the `if_vlan_var.h` / `if_cnmacvar.h` pattern). Content is unchanged. ERRATA E80; DESIGN §3 (components), §3.1 and §4 banners updated.

Verification: {{T1.0}} (hook sites compile with and without `pseudo-device flow`).

Fork commit `daa3e47c` ({{T1.0}}) follows it: `if_flow.h` holds only the hook API, `if_flowvar.h` the structures and MD ops. A hook-site test unit that includes only `flow.h` and `<net/if_flow.h>` compiles with and without flow (`tools/kcheck.py`). The real-build confirmation is part of {{T1.0}}'s Done-when. Closing.

issues.title: Finding: T1.1 needs a yield-rounding MD op and bounds for idle/budget/yield
issues.body:
**Finding (low), found while starting {{T1.1}}.** Two gaps between T1.1's Done-when and the interface documents.

1. **No way to learn the effective yield.** T1.1 requires: "Reading `yield` returns the effective value after rounding to the mechanism's granularity", and SPEC §6.1 says the same. The only MD scheduling operation in DESIGN §3.1 is `void (*fmo_sched_set)(u_int mode, u_int budget, u_int yield_us)`: it applies settings (and only during an active transition), and returns nothing. The MI sysctl code therefore cannot know the rounded value, least of all in mode 0, where nothing is applied.
2. **No bounds for three knobs.** T1.1 requires "bounds are enforced", but SPEC §6.1 gives values only for `mode` (0–3), `max` (1–4096) and `debug` (0/1). `idle` ("seconds"), `budget` ("WQEs per interrupt", 0 = unbounded) and `yield` ("microseconds") have none.

**Resolution.**

1. Add a pure MD operation `u_int (*fmo_yield_round)(u_int yield_us)` that returns the effective hold-off for a requested value (the mechanism's granularity, rounded up; no side effects). The setter stores the rounded value, so a read returns it in every mode. With no MD registered (amd64) the value is stored as given. DESIGN §3.1; ERRATA E81.
2. Bounds: `idle` 1–3600 s; `budget` 0–4096 (above the 768-buffer pool already means unbounded, and mode 2 may recycle buffers faster); `yield` 0–100000 µs (anything near 10 ms already overflows the PKT pool at 64-byte line rate, DESIGN §5.6). Default `yield` stays 0 until T0.9 sets it. SPEC §6.1; ERRATA E82.

Verification: {{T1.1}}.

comments.author: Claude Code (Opus 5.5)
comments.body: Resolved (repo commit `502c7d9`): ERRATA E81 (DESIGN §3.1 adds `u_int (*fmo_yield_round)(u_int)`) and E82 (SPEC §6.1 bounds: idle 1–3600 s, budget 0–4096, yield 0–100000 µs, yield default 0 until T0.9). Code follows in fork commit `e61f246b` ({{T1.1}}): `struct flow_md_ops` has the op; the yield setter stores the rounded value; `flow_sysctl()` enforces the bounds. Runtime confirmation is part of {{T1.1}}'s Done-when (`tests/t1.1-sysctl.sh`). Closing.

issues.title: Finding: SPEC §6.2 does not say which kstat holds which counter
issues.body:
**Finding (low), found while starting {{T1.2}}.**

SPEC §6.2 names three kstats — per port `cnmacN:0:flow`, global `flow:0:stats`, global `fpa:0:pools` — and then lists all counters in one table without saying which kstat holds which. T1.2 asks for "global kstat `flow:0:stats` with the SPEC §6.2 names", which read literally would put per-port hit-path counters (`hit`, `miss`, `sl_*`, …) in the global kstat, while {{T2.1}} creates `cnmacN:0:flow` for them. The `yield` counter is per RX group (one per CPU, shared by all ports), so it cannot be attributed to a port at all.

**Resolution** (SPEC §6.2 gets a "Kstat" column; ERRATA E83):

| Kstat | Counters | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `flow:0:stats` (global) | `lrn_*`, `ref_*`, `gen_*`, `gc_*`, `arp_refresh`, `arp_sweep_ms`, `yield` | MI `if_flow.c`; the MD RX loop counts `yield` through an MI helper |
| `cnmacN:0:flow` (per port) | `hit`, `miss`, `stale`, `sl_check`, `sl_ttl`, `sl_mtu`, `sl_dmac`, `sl_down` (ingress port), `txq_drop` (egress port) | MD, {{T2.1}}/{{T2.5}} |
| `fpa:0:pools` (global) | `fpa_pkt`, `fpa_wqe`, `fpa_cmd`, `fpa_sg` | MD, {{T2.1}} |

Verification: {{T1.2}} (flow:0:stats contents), {{T2.1}}.

issues.title: Finding: T1.3 placement gaps (PMTU writers, SIOCSTRUNK window, gate race)
issues.body:
**Finding (low), found while implementing {{T1.3}}.** Three gaps in DESIGN §5.4/§5.8, fixed in the same change (ERRATA E84–E86):

1. **PMTU writers.** DESIGN §5.4 listed `icmp_mtudisc()` and `tcp_subr.c`. At `c595b86dd344` `rt_mtu` has seven writers: `ip_icmp.c:1080, 1113`, `ip_output.c:474, 564`, `if_loop.c:269`, `rtsock.c:1331`, `route.c:564`. `tcp_subr.c` itself writes nothing; it calls `icmp_mtudisc()` (`tcp_subr.c:786`). Analysis of the rest (NOTES "T1.3 generation hook placements"): `rt_setgwroute()` (`route.c:564`) runs only from `rt_setgate()`, reached from bumped paths or from `rtredirect()`, and redirects are ignored while forwarding (`ip_icmp.c:594-597`); `ip_output.c:474` cannot change `min(rt_mtu, egress if_mtu)`; `:564` is IPsec-only; `if_loop.c` is loopback; `route_cleargateway()` sits on the RTF_CACHED delete path that also runs `arpinvalidate()`. Also, `RTM_CHANGE` can fail after editing a route in place (`bfdset()` after `rt_setgate()`, `rtsock.c:1125-1150`), so a success-only hook misses partial changes.
2. **SIOCSTRUNK window.** Changing a trunk's protocol clears `ac_trport` on every port and sets it again (`if_trunk.c:665, 687`). A commit in between passes the membership check (DESIGN §5.3 step 4); nothing bumped at the re-set.
3. **Gate race.** `flow_gate_update()` as specified recomputes from atomics and stores. Two updaters can interleave: A reads `ipsec_in_use` = 1 and computes 0; B (policy delete) computes 1 and stores; A stores 0. The gate stays closed, and HOOK B drops every request, until some unrelated policy change.

**Resolution:** hook `icmp_mtudisc()` only when its CAS changes the MTU, plus the timeout reset; `RTM_CHANGE` bumps at the end of `rtm_output()` for any change attempted on a found route; both `SIOCSTRUNK` loops bump; the gate is recomputed and stored under a leaf `flow_gate_mtx`. DESIGN §5.4 and §5.8 updated; ERRATA E84, E85, E86.

issues.title: Finding: DESIGN §7 bench and STOCK_TEST_PLAN topologies disagree
issues.body:
**Finding (medium), found while starting {{T0.3}}.** The two bench descriptions disagree, and SPEC §7.3 requires G0 and the fork to be measured with "the same hosts, routes, MTUs, LRO settings and traffic definitions".

- **DESIGN §7** bench: `cnmac0` = an OSPF neighbour router (real adjacency, route changes, TFTP/DHCP); `cnmac1` = VLAN trunk to the traffic hosts; `cnmac2` = untagged host and a second path to the neighbour (failover).
- **STOCK_TEST_PLAN.md §1–§2** (the G0 procedure {{T0.4}} uses): management on `cnmac0` only; traffic hosts A and B run FRR themselves and speak OSPF on the data ports; topologies U (A–cnmac1, cnmac2–B, untagged), V (vlan10/cnmac1, vlan20/cnmac2), H (vlan10 and vlan20 on one cnmac1 trunk through a switch); addresses 10.250.1.0/30, 10.250.2.0/30, test loopbacks 198.18.0.1 and 198.19.0.1.

A G0 measured on STOCK_TEST_PLAN's topology cannot be compared with fork runs on DESIGN §7's, and the two disagree about what `cnmac0` is.

**Resolution (ERRATA E87, DESIGN §7):** STOCK_TEST_PLAN §2 is the one measurement bench for G0, T2.10 and T3.4 (U, V, H); `cnmac0` stays management/TFTP. The OSPF failover, failback and ECMP-withdrawal tests of {{T2.7}} use topology F: U plus a second transit between B and the DUT, `vlan21` on `cnmac2` (10.250.3.0/30), so B advertises 198.19.0.1 over two OSPF paths and failover is driven by downing one path. No extra router is needed. The artefacts in `bench/` implement exactly this.

Owner: please confirm or say if a separate neighbour router on `cnmac0` is wanted after all (the scripts take the interface names from `bench/env.sh`).
